css-fundamentals-sr7-03.title: CSS Flexible Box Layout Module Level 1

css-fundamentals-sr1-10.reason: explanation_error: 'whose default behavior is to use its own value' is wrong. The new wording says the child receives the parent's computed value (MDN inherit: 'causes the element to take the computed value of the property from its parent element'). (final: keep)
css-fundamentals-sr1-10.statement: With `margin: inherit`, a child takes its parent's computed margin values.
css-fundamentals-sr1-10.explanation: The inherit keyword makes an element take the computed value of a property from its parent. Margin is a non-inherited property, so this keyword is how a child copies it.

css-fundamentals-sr1-09.reason: tell: breaks the 'restores an earlier/browser value' false template (3F, over the cap of 2) and removes the empty lead-in 'In ordinary block flow'. The fact and the answer (false) are unchanged. (final: keep)
css-fundamentals-sr1-09.statement: `display: initial` on a `div` gives it the browser's default `block` display.
css-fundamentals-sr1-09.explanation: The initial display value is inline. In ordinary flow, display: revert instead rolls back author styling and recovers the browser's block value for a div.
css-fundamentals-sr1-09.misconception: initial restores element-specific browser stylesheet values.

css-fundamentals-sr2-11.reason: source_problem: the Cascade 6 TR contains a note saying proximity applies 'regardless of specificity', which backs the opposite answer. MDN @scope says: 'Scoping proximity overrules source order but is itself overridden by other, higher-priority criteria such as importance, layers, and specificity.' The statement and explanation are unchanged. (final: keep)
css-fundamentals-sr2-11.statement: Within one author layer, scope proximity takes precedence over selector specificity.
css-fundamentals-sr2-11.explanation: The browser compares specificity before scope proximity. Proximity resolves competing declarations with equal specificity.
css-fundamentals-sr2-11.misconception: A nearer scope root overcomes a more specific competing selector.

css-fundamentals-sr3-12.reason: source_problem: the bare Cascade 5 root URL does not settle the card. MDN Specificity says it in one sentence: 'Styles for a directly targeted element will always take precedence over inherited styles, regardless of the specificity of the inherited rule.' The statement and explanation are unchanged. (final: keep)
css-fundamentals-sr3-12.statement: A `p` color declaration beats a color inherited from a parent's ID rule.
css-fundamentals-sr3-12.explanation: A declaration targeting the paragraph supplies its own color value. The parent's selector weight does not accompany an inherited value.

css-fundamentals-sr4-09.reason: ambiguous: 'a non-replaced box with one auto dimension' includes inline boxes and stretched flex items, where the ratio does nothing. The replacement is a concrete case that MDN confirms: 'At least one of the box's sizes needs to be automatic ... If neither the width nor height is an automatic size, then the provided aspect ratio has no effect'. MDN's own example uses a fixed width with height: auto. (final: keep)
css-fundamentals-sr4-09.statement: `aspect-ratio: 2 / 1` on an empty block `div` with `width: 300px` and `height: auto` gives it a 150px height.
css-fundamentals-sr4-09.explanation: With one automatic dimension, the browser derives it from the other through the ratio: 300px / 2 = 150px. When width and height are both set to lengths, aspect-ratio has no effect on the box.

css-fundamentals-sr5-01.reason: explanation_error: a flex container is block-level but not a 'block box', because it is not a block container. MDN: 'When we use display: flex we create a block-level container, with flex children', and its table maps flex to block flex. The statement is unchanged. (final: keep)
css-fundamentals-sr5-01.statement: `display: flex` gives an element a block-level outer display type in ordinary flow.
css-fundamentals-sr5-01.explanation: The flex keyword equals the multi-keyword value block flex: the outer type block makes the container block-level in its parent's flow, while the inner type flex lays out its children.

source.title: Using the multi-keyword syntax with CSS display

css-fundamentals-sr6-02.reason: tell: 'as its containing block' appeared only in false statements (sr6-02, sr6-03, sr6-04). This rewrite removes it here and also cleans up the awkward explanation. The fact (padding box, not content box) and the answer (false) are unchanged. (final: keep)
css-fundamentals-sr6-02.statement: An absolute child of a `position: relative` block is positioned against that parent's content box.
css-fundamentals-sr6-02.explanation: An absolutely positioned box's containing block is the padding box of its nearest positioned ancestor, so its offsets are measured from inside the border, padding included.
css-fundamentals-sr6-02.misconception: An absolute child's containing block excludes its positioned parent's padding.

css-fundamentals-sr6-03.reason: tell: second removal of the false-only phrase 'as its containing block'. The fact (a transformed ancestor becomes the fixed box's containing block) and the answer (false) are unchanged. (final: keep)
css-fundamentals-sr6-03.statement: A fixed child of a block with `transform: translateX(10px)` is positioned relative to the viewport.
css-fundamentals-sr6-03.explanation: The transformed block establishes the containing block for its fixed child, so the child is positioned relative to that block.
css-fundamentals-sr6-03.misconception: Fixed positioning retains a viewport containing block inside a transformed ancestor.

css-fundamentals-sr6-07.reason: ambiguous: 'uses its nearest ancestor' did not say for what, and the natural 'containing block' reading is false. The new statement names the role. The verifier's text was not used as written because it had 'even when' (a concession tell) and 'without' (a negation). MDN position: 'a sticky element "sticks" to its nearest ancestor that has a "scrolling mechanism" (created when overflow is hidden, scroll, auto, or overlay), even if that ancestor isn't the nearest actually scrolling ancestor.' (final: fixed)
css-fundamentals-sr6-07.statement: A sticky box in an `overflow: hidden` ancestor with nothing to scroll sticks to that ancestor instead of the viewport.
css-fundamentals-sr6-07.explanation: Sticky positioning attaches to the nearest ancestor with a scrolling mechanism (overflow hidden, scroll, auto or overlay), even if that ancestor never actually scrolls.

css-fundamentals-sr6-12.reason: tell: concession clauses ('even when', 'despite') marked only true cards. This removes 'even when'. The fact and the answer (true) are unchanged. (final: keep)
css-fundamentals-sr6-12.statement: `isolation: isolate` creates a stacking context for a block whose `z-index` is `auto`.
css-fundamentals-sr6-12.explanation: The isolate value explicitly establishes a stacking context, independently of the block's z-index.

css-fundamentals-sr7-03.reason: source_problem: Basic concepts does not state the auto-size, margin or min/max conditions. Flexbox 1 #align-items-property does: 'If the cross size property of the flex item computes to auto, and neither of the cross-axis margins are auto, the flex item is stretched ... while still respecting the constraints imposed by min-height/min-width/max-height/max-width.' The vague 'fixed margins' is replaced by a concrete row case. The verifier's 'no auto' wording was avoided because it is a negation. (final: keep)
css-fundamentals-sr7-03.statement: By default, a row flex item with `height: auto` and zero margins stretches to its flex line's height.
css-fundamentals-sr7-03.explanation: The initial align-items value is stretch: an item whose cross size computes to auto and whose cross-axis margins are not auto fills the line, within its min and max sizes.

source.title: CSS Flexible Box Layout Module Level 1

css-fundamentals-sr7-05.reason: ambiguous: the card hinged on 0% versus 0, and the spec (flex-common: flex: <number> = <number> 1 0) has reverted 0% to 0. The card now tests zero versus auto, which holds under both MDN ('flex-basis is then equal to 0%'; flex: auto = 1 1 auto) and the spec. (final: keep)
css-fundamentals-sr7-05.statement: `flex: 1` sets a flex item's flex-basis to zero instead of auto.
css-fundamentals-sr7-05.explanation: A single unitless number sets flex-grow to that number, flex-shrink to 1 and flex-basis to zero (MDN writes 0%). The keyword flex: auto keeps the auto basis instead.

css-fundamentals-sr8-04.reason: weak_card (near-copy of the MDN sentence). Rewritten instead of dropped: dropping all three weak r8 true cards would leave 3T/6F. MDN repeat(): auto-fit collapses empty repeated tracks after placement, and 'A collapsed track is treated as having a single fixed track sizing function of 0px, and the gutters on either side of it collapse'. The 1fr tracks then share the freed leftover space (flex_value: fr is 'a fraction of the leftover space'). (final: keep)
css-fundamentals-sr8-04.statement: With `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(100px, 1fr))`, two items in a wide container stretch across the full row.
css-fundamentals-sr8-04.explanation: auto-fit collapses repeated tracks still empty after placement to 0px, along with their gutters, so the two filled 1fr tracks share the freed space.

css-fundamentals-sr10-08.reason: ambiguous: the current Houdini editor's draft makes all @property descriptors optional, so 'syntax and inherits required' could flip. Replaced with the stable scoped fact. MDN var(): 'If the custom property is registered with @property using a non-universal syntax and an initial-value, that initial value is substituted when no other declaration applies. The fallback is not used in that case.' 'Set nowhere' rules out a value inherited from a parent, and the wording avoids the verifier's 'without' (a negation). (final: fixed)
css-fundamentals-sr10-08.statement: For an undeclared `--gap` registered as `<length>` with an initial-value, `var(--gap, 1rem)` returns that initial-value.
css-fundamentals-sr10-08.explanation: A registered property with a non-universal syntax and an initial-value substitutes that initial value when no other declaration applies, so var() leaves the 1rem fallback unused.

css-fundamentals-sr12-12.reason: ambiguous: 'equivalent color values' over-generalised beyond the sRGB forms MDN shows. The new card uses MDN's exact case: 'other color values equivalent to sRGB blue (such as the hexadecimal code #0000ff) will match only if the --accent-color property was defined as a color with @property'. For unregistered properties, 'The match is essentially a comparison of the two values' tokens.' The statement was shortened to keep r12's true/false length gap under 5. (final: keep)
css-fundamentals-sr12-12.explanation: Registering the property with <color> syntax lets style() treat equivalent values as a match, so blue, #00f and rgb(0 0 255) all match. Unregistered, the tokens are compared as written.

css-fundamentals-sr13-05.reason: tell: breaks the false equivalence template 'the same X as ... in Y'. It also fixes r13's length tell: after the two true drops, true cards averaged 8.7 characters shorter than false ones, and the gap is now 4.0. The fact (oklch() and hsl() hue angles differ) and the answer (false) are unchanged. MDN oklch: 'The hue angles in oklch() are different from those in hsl().' (final: fixed)
css-fundamentals-sr13-05.statement: `oklch()` and `hsl()` share one hue wheel for their hue angles.
css-fundamentals-sr13-05.explanation: Hue angles differ between color spaces: hsl() works in sRGB while oklch() works in Oklab, so the same angle can name a different hue in each function.
css-fundamentals-sr13-05.misconception: oklch() hue angles map to the same hues as hsl() hue angles.

css-fundamentals-sr14-12.reason: ambiguous: 'applies ... before' can be read in written order or in geometric order. The new statement is an equivalence that both readings agree on. css-transforms-2 #ctm: identity, translate by transform-origin, then translate, rotate, scale, then 'Multiply by each of the transform functions in transform property from left to right', then translate by the negated origin. So translate: 50px plus transform: rotate(45deg) equals transform: translate(50px) rotate(45deg). (final: keep)
css-fundamentals-sr14-12.statement: `translate: 50px` with `transform: rotate(45deg)` renders like `transform: translate(50px) rotate(45deg)`.
css-fundamentals-sr14-12.explanation: The browser composes translate, rotate and scale first, then multiplies in the transform list, so the individual properties act as if written to the left of the transform functions.
